=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh:91-111,148-155 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `fail()` can write a label and comment to the payload-specified target issue when validation fails before the dispatcher's authority is checked.
  WHY: An unauthorized dispatcher can send a malformed payload naming an issue and cause writes to that issue, contrary to the stated goal that a refused dispatch writes nothing to the target issue.
- scripts/claude_issue_route.py:15 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `DISPATCHER_ALLOWED_PERMISSIONS` omits the `maintain` permission.
  WHY: GitHub returns `maintain` for maintain-role collaborators, so they are refused with `dispatcher_not_authorized`.
- scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh:108-109 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `fail()` unconditionally appends `Run: ${RUN_URL}` to its Telegram error message, leaving a bare `Run: ` line when `RUN_URL` is empty.
  WHY: Hand-driven runs with an empty `RUN_URL` produce a malformed Telegram error message, unlike the guarded `reject()` implementation.
- scripts/claude_issue_intake.sh:33 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The `error_tail` Python one-liner can emit a very long unsplit line from the last 300 bytes.
  WHY: Long error details can cause `tg_send_msg` to truncate or fail, producing a malformed Telegram error on hand-driven runs.
